feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at the same organization support leadership growth and domain expertise.  
- Strong strategic + technical positioning: combines communications leadership with Drupal/CMS, analytics, workflow, and multimedia capabilities.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and newsletter reach all add weight.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results, not just responsibilities: include outcome metrics such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, production efficiency, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to avoid redundancy and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); standardize hyphenation (“cross-channel”/“Multi-channel,” “organization-wide”). No obvious misspellings; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specificity, a more concise opening, and less overlap with the competencies/skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and fix grammar: use “12+ years of experience.”
- Emphasize seniority and sector relevance by naming public-sector, advocacy, or mission-driven communications earlier.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with concrete value: leading platform modernization, cross-channel strategy, and operational systems.
- Keep the intro high-level; save channel lists and detailed capabilities for skills and experience sections.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience advancing web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content and aligning stakeholders around high-impact communications.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and operational strengths, but several items are broad or overlap heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership themes will make this section sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS and web platform administration,” “Editorial systems and workflow design.”
- Reduce repetition by combining overlapping items: merge “Editorial workflow design” with “Workflow & systems architecture,” and simplify “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” to “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Align style and parallel structure; use either all nouns or all noun phrases. Example rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS & web platform administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider adding “Governance” if space allows, since it is a recurring strength in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” and “policy/advocacy communication” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This block also overlaps with Topline Skills, especially analytics, workflow systems, and multimedia.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten around 3–5 highest-value contributions and add outcomes, scale, or complexity.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and content operations modernization.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, redesigned, implemented, streamlined, launched, optimized.
- Combine overlapping bullets and add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/templates, users, stakeholders, turnaround time reduced, publishing efficiency gained, search relevance/engagement improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, creating reusable microsite templates, modular content components, and member toolkit workflows to speed publishing and improve consistency across public-facing properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, workflows, governance, analytics” repeats language already used in the summary and NACo roles.
- CMS/front-end troubleshooting may be too tactical unless tied to business impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform detail and scale. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and make the result explicit: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on analytics/governance: “Built an enterprise analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for email/social/video/budget: audience growth, engagement lift, production savings, faster publishing, reduced vendor spend.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video studio creation may partially overlap with earlier multimedia bullets—frame it here as capacity-building and organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story within NACo, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or production outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and supporting advocacy messaging to county officials nationwide.”
- Tighten bullets to focus on owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership if accurate: “Standardized publishing workflows and editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify what was newly expanded or formalized here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it more distinctive by sharpening the leadership angle and tying it to enterprise-scale governance and mission-driven/public-sector work.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy and communications transformation
- Editorial governance, publishing operations, and content systems
- Cross-channel team leadership across web, email, social, and multimedia
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy and information architecture
- If space allows, swap one line for a scale cue drawn from recent roles, e.g. “Enterprise web and content leadership for 10,000+ page platforms and 50+ publishers.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience: use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel,” and “audience-centered” instead of “audience-focused.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communication” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design”; differentiate by emphasizing governance/operations.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented line: **Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems design • AI-enabled search and content discovery**
- Remove lower-priority or older platform names here unless they are central to current targeting; keep **Drupal** first because it is most supported by recent experience.
- Drop **jQuery** from topline skills; it feels dated and can stay in Technical + IT if needed.
- Consider replacing **Power Pages** or **SharePoint** with a stronger capability phrase like **structured content architecture** or **microsite and modular page builds** if those better reflect recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the **Technical + IT** section; keep topline skills capability-based and reserve tool lists for Technical + IT.
- **AI-enabled search experiences** already appears in recent consulting experience, so keep it only if it supports the target role.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating tools already proven in the NACo experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Digital analytics & optimization” with grouped skills.
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • SEO, content, and performance analysis”
- If space allows, make the outcome clearer: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, and executive reporting for web performance, audience insights, and optimization”
- Keep only the most relevant platforms here; let work experience demonstrate implementation depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role; consider trimming this line if space is tight.
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so emphasize optimization or executive insight here instead.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster and relevant to your recent NACo leadership work, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to the studio/build-out and event formats you’ve led.

Suggested edit:

- Replace generic bullets with sharper phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera systems and studio operations
- Virtual event execution and technical run-of-show coordination
- If space allows, add one higher-level capability instead of a basic task, e.g. “In-house studio buildout and production workflow design”
- Keep terms consistent with recent roles; “broadcast-quality” aligns well with the NACo studio achievement

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; consider trimming one or differentiating this section as execution-focused
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine to avoid repetition

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but as written it’s just a duplicate of the stronger “Topline Skills” section. This item should either add specificity on level of use/recent relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same CMS names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest, most recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of a bare list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing: GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it reflects meaningful recent work; it reads less central than Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV and prioritize platforms tied to quantified achievements already shown in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same CMS tools.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so this item should add nuance, not just repeat names.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and aligned to the hands-on work shown in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter, grouped list: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- If accurate, modernize phrasing by dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) to “HTML, CSS” unless ATS targeting specifically benefits from versions.
- Consider adding one brief qualifier for level/scope, e.g., “Front-end implementation for Drupal-based sites, tagging, automation, and lightweight serverless workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or consolidate.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap with “Workflow automation”; avoid repeating automation language across both sections.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a generic tool dump. Since workflow architecture is already emphasized elsewhere, this line should be tightened and framed around systems most relevant to recent work, separating true automation tools from collaboration/project platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If you have stronger evidence from recent roles, consider replacing weaker/older tools with a qualifier: **Airtable systems, workflow automation, project coordination platforms**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if this section needs breadth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email-platform leadership. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and enterprise systems, frame these as platforms you’ve administered or used to run member communications.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign deployment, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications)**
- If accurate, strengthen further with scope: **…supporting newsletters and campaigns reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep only the strongest/current tools; order by relevance to recent work, with Dynamics 365 first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating audience scale here if it already appears prominently in recent roles
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications” language elsewhere

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce channel list repetition: “improved publishing workflows and supported web, email, social, and video operations.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience/reach, event support volume.
- Suggested rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving publishing workflows and supporting web, email, social, and video operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating governance/strategy language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the innovation/research scope and keep the digital piece concise.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground coordination and the standout launch: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the media portion: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Consider a two-part structure: innovation/research first, podcast second, to show breadth without overexplaining.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter on general media language.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities here unless they were distinct and measurable.
